commits.message:
fix(table): measure the cells the flags say are drawn (rich-table-8c8)

`_naturalWidth` sized a column against the wrong set of cells at both ends: it
seeded from the header unconditionally and never looked at `col.footer` at all.

The footer half lost data. A footer wider than everything above it got no column
wide enough to hold it, so a totals row — exactly the case where the footer is
the widest cell in its column — rendered as `…`. The header half wasted width:
a column was sized to header text `showHeader: false` had told the table not to
draw.

One rule, not two fixes. The reference's `_get_cells` appends the header cell
under `show_header` and the footer cell under `show_footer`, and both
`_measure_column` and `_render` iterate it — the measured cells ARE the drawn
cells. This port enumerated that set a second time inside the width path, and a
second enumeration is what let the two ends disagree with the draw path and with
each other.

`_columnCells` is now that enumeration, and the measuring loop lost its special
case with it: the header was a seed measured by a different expression than the
body cells, which is the same asymmetry that produced rich-table-n27 one
constructor line away. All three positions now flow through one `Math.max` over
one sequence, and membership is a flag rather than a guard.

Both reference frames pinned as tests, both red without this change. 2306 pass,
`table-frames.golden.txt` unmoved and untouched, three-pass lint and the demo
typecheck clean.

Filed while here, verified pre-existing by restoring master's table.ts and
re-probing: rich-table-3d3, a rowless table sizes to its header instead of
filling the offer, because `_naturalWidth`'s single number cannot say "no cells
to measure" distinctly from "measures zero" where Rich returns Measurement(1,1).

fix(table): let the flag alone decide the header and footer rows (rich-table-n27) (#103)

Rich draws these rows on `show_header` / `show_footer` and nothing else. This
port additionally required some column to have content, so a table that asked
for a row silently did not get one and nothing reported it. `showFooter: true`
with no footers anywhere drew no footer row at all; a table whose headers were
all blank lost two lines rather than one, because the guard sat above the head
separator as well as the row it was about.

The guards were the symptom. `Column.footer` was `RichText | undefined` where
Rich declares `footer: RenderableType = ""`, and that optional is what made
`some((c) => c.footer)` a well-typed, plausible-reading expression in the first
place. It also forced a `?? toCellText(undefined)` at the use site — an inland
guard compensating for the same missing constraint. Absent and empty are the
same footer, so `footer` is now built by the same one-liner as `header` one line
above it, and the two fields answer to the same question.

The asymmetry between those two constructor lines is what gave the bug away.
It also explains why the two footerless spellings disagreed with each other and
not only with the reference: `footer: ""` produced a truthy empty `RichText` and
unlocked the row, while no footer at all left it `undefined` and did not. The
drawing code was already correct and already matched the reference frame
character for character — only the guard deciding whether to reach it was wrong,
which is why the fix removes code rather than adding any.

Measured against Python Rich at width 20 across five shapes; all five now match
character for character. Four are pinned: the footer row with no footer, absent
and empty footers rendering identically, the blank-header row with its
separator, and `showHeader: false` still suppressing a header that has content —
that last one passes on the old code too and is there to catch over-correction,
not to pin the fix. The other three fail without it. `table-frames.golden.txt`
and the sentinel-grid test are unmoved, as is every other frame in the suite:
2304 pass, and no existing table has a blank header or asks for a footer row it
has no footers for, which is exactly why this survived.

Filed rich-table-76o while adjacent: `_naturalWidth` measures the header
unconditionally and never measures the footer, where the reference measures each
one exactly when its flag says it will be drawn. A long footer is ellipsized to
a single cell. Not caused or widened by this change — the footer rows it newly
draws are blank in every column, so there is nothing in them to truncate.
